points.description: States that both iteration and recursion involve repetition (repeatedly executing a set of instructions/process), using this idea precisely.
States that both have termination tests (iteration has a loop-continuation test; recursion has a base case) and that each ends when its test is met.
points.partial_credit: 1 mark if says both terminate/end but does not identify a termination test (loop condition / base case) for both.

points.description: States that both can occur infinitely (iteration: infinite loop if the continuation test never becomes false; recursion: infinite recursion if the base case is never reached).

rubric.notes: Full marks need all three similarities stated precisely: repetition, termination tests, and the possibility of infinite execution. Each point is earned only if clearly and correctly stated; vague or merely implied statements earn nothing. Any wrong claim about a point (e.g. saying recursion has no termination test) earns nothing for that point. Differences between the two earn no marks.
